source: ACIAR AH/2005/086 'Smallholder Cattle Best Practice Manual' (Windsor, Bush & Young), Best Practice Health and Husbandry of Cattle, Cambodia -- hosted at mekonglivestock.wordpress.com (University of Sydney / GDAHP project site)
text: On selling cattle, the manual advises farmers to think about which market they are targeting -- local, domestic, or export -- since each has different requirements around age, body condition score, sex, and weight, and some traders buy specifically for certain markets. It recommends selling only when an animal is genuinely 'market ready' rather than purely as a cash source, since value-adding (e.g. fattening) before sale increases returns, and targeting sale timing around festivals like the New Year (when prices run higher) can improve income; using forage technology and silage/irrigation can help extend the beef season beyond the wet season. The manual also suggests farmers coordinate sale timing and use defined selling days/locations to increase their collective market power against middlemen/traders.
